records.quote: Example 2.1. Let X have the Pareto type II survival function F̄_X(t) = (1 + t/β)^{−α}, t ≥ 0, where α > 1 and β > 0. Then X has unbounded support, E(X) = β/(α − 1) < ∞, and µ_X(t) = (β + t)/(α − 1), tµ′_X(t)/µ_X(t) = t/(β + t) → 1 as t → ∞. Thus, the assumptions of Theorem 2.7 are satisfied with ρ = 1. Moreover, A_X(t) = (βt + t²/2)/(α − 1), L^µ_X(t) = tµ_X(t)/A_X(t) = 2(β + t)/(2β + t) → 2 = 1 + ρ as t → ∞.

records.quote: Theorem 2.12. Let {X_θ : θ > 0} be a proportional hazards family with survival functions F̄_θ(t) = {F̄_0(t)}^θ, 0 ≤ t < τ_0, and let H_0(t) = −log F̄_0(t). If H_0 is positive and differentiable on (0, τ_0), then L_θ(t) = L_0(t), 0 < t < τ_0. Hence, the FRAI function is invariant under the proportional hazards family.

records.ambiguity: Equality characterization rather than a strict ordering; it underpins the antisymmetry discussion of ≤_MRLAI on p.40 (with µ_X(0+) = µ_Y(0+) and τ_X = τ_Y it yields identical distributions).

note: Two-distribution iff claim giving the equality case of the paper's ≤_MRLAI order — kept; differs from the excluded §2 characterizations.
Single-distribution characterization (constant MRLAI iff exponential) for a general lifetime distribution — 'result that only characterizes one distribution' per the spec; out of scope.

DMRL ⇒ L^µ_X ≤ 1 plus a printed piecewise-MRL counterexample to the converse — a single-distribution characterization for arbitrary lifetimes, out of spec scope; the embedded counterexample distribution reappears as Counterexample 4.1 (already canonical).
IMRL ⇒ L^µ_X ≥ 1 with a printed converse counterexample — same single-distribution characterization scope as Theorem 2.5; out of scope.
X ∈ DMRLA iff L^µ_X ≤ 1 (resp. IMRLA iff ≥ 1) — iff characterization of one distribution's class membership, no ordering conclusion; out of scope.
DMRLAI iff A_X geometrically concave (IMRLAI iff convex) — structural characterization of a single distribution, no ordering conclusion; out of scope.

records.quote: Theorem 3.1. Let n ≥ 1, and let X1, . . . , Xn be i.i.d. absolutely continuous lifetime random variables over the support with common differentiable survival function F̄_X, and MRL function µ_X(t) = a + bt, 0 ≤ t < τ_X, where a > 0 and b > −1. If X_{1:n} = min{X1, . . . , Xn}, then L^µ_{X_{1:n}}(t) = L^µ_X(t), 0 < t < τ_X.
records.family: iid components, linear MRL µ_X = a + bt (a > 0, b > −1)
records.compared: series-system lifetime X_{1:n} vs component lifetime X under the MRLAI function

hypotheses.text: Xi iid absolutely continuous, differentiable F̄_X, µ_X = a + bt with a > 0, b > −1

conclusion.direction: L^µ_{X_{1:n}}(t) = L^µ_X(t) for all n ≥ 1 — series system is MRLAI-equal to its component (equality case of ≤_MRLAI)

records.quantifiers: n ≥ 1; 0 < t < τ_X (τ_X = −a/b when b < 0; infinite when b ≥ 0)
records.ambiguity: Exact invariance only within the linear-MRL family — the text notes preservation of DMRLAI/IMRLAI follows for this family; the general DMRLAI class is not closed under series systems (Counterexample 3.3).

note: Printed on p.32; relational equality between system and component lifetimes under the MRLAI function within a specific family — in scope.
